text:
devon: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change rolled to canary (canary-42) we're seeing cross-zone spillovers spike for eu-west. Latency tail worsened for small chats. repro: 10-20% increase in P95 on p50 token workloads.

li: saw that in dashboards. kv cache hit rate dropped ~8% at the same time. Might be warmup mismatch when kernel switches mid-KV-warmup.

sara: can you paste the canary config? curious about batching window + token_budget_target.

devon: config excerpt from canary:```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_ms: 12
  min_fill_tokens: 8
  token_budget_target: 512
  allow_cross_zone_spill: true
  affinity: PREFER_LOCAL
```

kai: token_budget_target 512 seems high for short-conversation workload. That increases batching time for small reqs and raises chance of spilling when local queues are shallow. Also kernel handoff timing changed; we now pick kernel B for seq_len <=128 which has slightly different prefix handling.

devon: exact symptom: local GPU queues drain faster but we push overflow to nearest zone rather than waiting ~3ms extra to fill smaller batches. net effect: more cross-zone RPCs and worse P95.

perf-bot: [auto] alert: region eu-west - cross-zone RPCs increased 3.1x in last 15m.

li: proposal: reduce token_budget_target for small-instance families and add a per-region emergency backoff that prefers waiting up to X ms instead of spilling. e.g. if estimated spill latency > 5ms prefer local drain.

sara: +1. Also add a KV warmup bias so kernel selection doesn't flip to a variant that disables our fast prefix merge until cache hit stabilizes.

kai: quick experiment patch:```diff
-continuous_batcher:
-  token_budget_target: 512
+continuous_batcher:
+  token_budget_target: 256
+  max_spill_wait_ms: 6  # prefer waiting for local fill when cross-zone penalized
+  kernel_stability_window_ms: 40  # avoid switching kernels until warmup
```

devon: running that on canary-43 now (region eu-west only). Added metric: spill_wait_rate and kernel_flip_count.

li: initial 10m smoke: P95 down ~6% vs canary-42, kv hit rate creeping back up, cross-zone RPCs down 40%. looks promising.

sara: any regression on throughput? we need to keep cost bound.

devon: CPU overhead up ~1.2% due to holding requests; throughput flat. cost model suggests slight token-cost increase but network egress saved by avoiding cross-zone RPCs.

kai: note for rollout: we should gate max_spill_wait_ms by customer tier + region. enterprise customers might prefer lower latency even if cross-zone used. default behavior should be cost-aware.

li: added a small tracing snippet to help debug next time:```json
{"trace_id":"t-9843","kernel":"B","kv_hit":false,"queue_wait_ms":5,"spill":true}
```

devon: action items: 1) keep canary-43 for 2h, 2) gather 95/99 latencies, kv hit trajectories, and cross-zone counts, 3) run a quick perf regression against batch-heavy synthetic workload.

sara: I'll own 3). kai can you draft rollout gating (region + customer tier + kernel-stability threshold)?

kai: on it. will add a simple flag `prefer_local_on_spill_penalty` and a decider that checks estimated spill penalty > threshold.

perf-bot: [auto] metric snapshot: canary-43 (10m): cross-zone RPCs -40%, P95 -6%, kv_hit +4%.

devon: sweet. if numbers hold we'll push to 25% of traffic in eu-west tomorrow morning. any objections?

li: none from me. just monitor for hidden regressions (cold-starts, long conversations).

sara: also run kernel microbench after 24h to ensure no perf regression in kernel B for medium sequences.

devon: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
